Hi Diego —

Hope you’re well. Our AP team ran NV-0421 and noticed two issues:

1) Marketplace commission line (line 3) appears to have been billed at 6.5% instead of the 3.5% we agreed for the promo period (Apr–May).

We’d like Redwood to (a) reissue corrected invoicing or credit the overcharged commission, and (b) confirm how you want us to evidence the withholding so it’s not treated as a disputed balance on your side. Can you propose how to split the credit and what docs you need for tax/withholding clearance?

Hi Marta —

Thanks for flagging this — I’m sorry for the hassle. High level proposal:

- We’ll split the remedy into two items so accounting lines are clear:
  1) A service-credit covering the overcharged commission amount (this will correct your invoice value).
  2) A withholding/tds adjustment memo to reflect the tax retained by your AP team so our ledger reconciles to the net you actually paid.

To proceed we’ll need:
- Confirmation of the agreed promo commission (3.5% for Apr–May) and the calculation showing the overcharged amount (line-level math).
- A copy of the TDS certificate or a letter from your tax office (if available) OR the remittance advice that shows 10% was withheld.
- Whether you prefer the credit to be (A) applied against this invoice immediately, or (B) issued as a credit memo to be applied to next month’s invoice.

I’ve looped in Prioym and Laura from Finance to draft the two credit memos and confirm tax handling. We’ll aim to produce a draft credit memo for your review within 48 business hours once we have the docs above.

Best,
Diego Fernández
Account Executive — Enterprise Revenue Operations

Diego / team —

Thanks for the context. From an accounting perspective here’s the cleanest path we can take so both parties reconcile:

1) Create two credit memos:
   - Credit A (Service Credit): reverses the overcharged commission amount; non-taxable in our books since it’s a pricing correction to an expense line.
   - Credit B (Withholding Adjustment): documents the 10% TDS withheld by Nivora to match the net remitted amount. This will be listed on our side as a tax-withheld note; we’ll include the payer (Nivora) tax ID and the withholding percentage in the memo.

2) Required evidence: either the TDS certificate or the remittance advice showing the tax withheld + a short confirmation email from you stating that Nivora requests the withholding be recognized as tax withheld at source.

3) Tax treatment note: If Nivora is able to provide a local tax certificate showing the payment is tax-exempt or eligible for credit, we’ll record the withholding adjustment as recoverable pending documentation. If not, we’ll tag the withholding as an AP variance and add a short explanatory note on the memo.

Laura — can you please draft the two memos and set up the credit numbers? I’ll confirm GL accounts and whether we should issue a single combined credit memo with two lines vs two separate memos.

Prioym
Sr. Revenue Accountant, Redwood
